title: Pushed colorful polytopal KKMS Theorem and orthogonal star transversals
summary: A classical theorem of Kaiser and Rabinovich implies that if every subfamily of size at most $\lfloor\log_2(d+1)\rfloor+1$ of a finite family of compact connected sets in $\mathbb{R}^d$ has a common axis-parallel hyperplane transversal, then the entire family has an orthogonal star transversal, i.e., a union of $d$ hyperplanes, one perpendicular to each coordinate axis. We study colorful variants of this result. First, we use standard KKM machinery to establish a colorful analogue with $d+1$ color classes and a $\lfloor\log_2(d+1)\rfloor+1$ transversal hypothesis for rainbow subfamiles. Then…
